data.narrative:
The Bot Company is a Series B robotics and manufacturing platform founded by Kyle Vogt, Paril Jain, and Luke Holoubek, having raised approximately $550M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of four same-sector peers at Series B and adjacent Series C stages, supplemented by a broader set of eight private robotics companies and one public comparable.

Peer-median analysis, the primary applicable method, identifies a median valuation of $1.6B across four direct comparables: Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), Hadrian ($1.6B, Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B, Series C). This method establishes the central reference point given the target's stage and sector alignment with three of four peers.

The triangulated valuation range is $1.4B to $1.9B, anchored to the $1.6B peer median. Key uncertainties include limited methodological diversification—only peer-median triangulation is applicable given available data—and stage-mixing within the comparable set, with two peers at Series C versus two at Series B. The analysis is particularly sensitive to company-specific execution risk, market adoption trajectory, and capital efficiency relative to the peer cohort, none of which are quantified in available data.
